content: I prostrate to and take refuge in the great master, the second Buddha, in all ways and at all times.Of all the thousand Buddhas who appear in this Fortunate Aeon,Equal in their abandonment, realization, and compassion for beings,Yet here in this land of snow mountains, there is no one equal to you;Contemplating your inexpressible kindness, my faith increases.In this Land of Snows, the Lotus-Bearer,Prophesied by the Victors to tame beings—Other than the life-stories enacted by the three Ancestral Kings and the Great One of Orgyen,There is nothing else to be found."Meditate on me, the Guru; accomplish me; follow in my footsteps.To see me is to see all the Buddhas; since I myselfAm the very essence of all the Sugatas gathered as one,"You said, "I shall appear in Tibet every time the tenth day comes."Therefore, remembering your life story, I pray to you.At sunrise on the tenth day of the sixth lunar month,You appeared within the hollow of a lotus on Lake Dhanakośa.In the month of Gyal, invited by King Indrabhūti,You were enthroned as prince and attained the supreme Vajra path.In the month of Chu, you renounced the kingdom to seek the Cool Grove,And through your yogic conduct, you brought the ḍākinīs under your command.In the month of Phalguna, to lead beings gradually into the teachings,You took ordination from the master Prabhahasti.In the month of Chaitra, when the King of Zahor attempted to burn you alive,You transformed the fire into water and were praised by the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three.In the month of Vaishakha, when the King of Orgyen sought to burn the Father and Mother,Even those with perverted desires, who should have been burned together,You placed, beyond their own control, into a state of faith.In the month of Jyeṣṭha, in the kingdoms of the southern frontier,You liberated with thunderbolts the heretics who were hostile to the teachings.In the month of Śrāvaṇa, in the border land of Tāmradvīpa,When the heretic king placed you inside a large copper vessel with its lid sealed,And cast you into the river, through your miraculous power,You instantly ascended into the sky, and at that very moment, the riverFlowed backward, threatening the palace of the sinful king,Who, overwhelmed with terror, apologized and took refuge in you.In the month of Bhadrapada, when evil heretics offered poisoned food,You were unharmed, and even beyond that,You displayed a state of even more radiant and flourishing splendor.In the month of Ashvina, you traveled to Yangleshö;Although the gods and demons of both Nepal and Tibet challenged you,Arising in the form of Vajrakumāra, you bound them under oath.In the month of Smin-drug, you arrived in Central Tibet.On the peak of Mount Hepori, you bound the gods and demons under oath.That the Buddha's teachings spread in Tibet is due to your kindness alone;Reflecting on how this is not dependent on any other, I feel deep faith.In the month of Mgo-zla, intending to depart for the land of the rakshasas,At Chimphu, the master and patrons conferred, and as a preparationTo fill the entire land of Tibet with hidden treasures,You subjugated the local spirits and entrusted them with the treasure inventories.Therefore, on every tenth day that occurs,This is the festival of your enlightened deeds and activities,And the occasion when the mothers and dakinis assemble;Internally, through the marvelous interdependence of the gatheringOf the channels, essences, and winds within the vajra body,Mastery is gained over all four types of enlightened activity.May rain fall in season, and may diseases and epidemics affecting humans and livestock be pacified.Frost, hail, poverty, warfare, loss of livestock, and so forth—All the various forms of worldly decline and the degenerations of the age—If you offer prayers while maintaining the Tenth Day offerings,These will be tangibly pacified through that blessing alone.The time to fulfill your promise has come; look upon us with compassion!All the mindful people of Tibet have faith in you.Even toward those mindless ones who act with hostilityToward their own kind parents, we invoke your compassion,Which is free from partiality; we urge you to fulfill your sacred vow.Never forsaking the Tibetan people,The time to fulfill your promise has come; look upon us with compassion!Grant your blessings so that all intentions are fulfilled according to our wishes.This was written by Rig-’dzin ’Jigs-med gling-pa for the one named Dbyangs-yig dang-po of Samye Rabjung.
